name: INDIRECT
description: INDIRECT converts a text string into a cell reference that Excel can use in a formula.
tldr: Turns text that looks like a cell reference into an actual reference.

parameters.name: ref_text
parameters.description: A text string that describes a cell reference or named range.

parameters.name: a1
parameters.description: If TRUE, ref_text is interpreted in A1 style. If FALSE, R1C1 style. Default is TRUE.

basicExample.explanation: The text "A1" is converted to the cell reference A1.

advancedExamples.title: Dynamic sheet reference
advancedExamples.description: Pull a value from a sheet named in cell B2
advancedExamples.explanation: If B2 contains "Sheet2", the formula references Sheet2!A1.

advancedExamples.title: Dynamic named range
advancedExamples.description: Sum a named range selected from a dropdown
advancedExamples.explanation: A2 contains a named range name, and INDIRECT converts it to a reference for SUM.

howItWorks: INDIRECT takes a text string and evaluates it as a cell reference. This allows dynamic references based on formulas or user input. However, the resulting reference is not updated when cells move or insert.

howToSteps.name: Build reference text
howToSteps.text: Create a string that looks like a cell reference, e.g. "A1" or "Sheet2!B2".

howToSteps.name: Use the reference
howToSteps.text: Use it inside other functions like SUM, VLOOKUP, etc.

limitations: Volatile: recalculates whenever the workbook changes, which can slow down large workbooks.
Does not update if rows/columns are inserted or deleted.
A1 parameter defaults to TRUE (A1 style).

commonErrors.cause: The text string is not a valid reference or the sheet does not exist.
commonErrors.fix: Verify the text string and sheet names.

commonErrors.cause: Sheet names with spaces need single quotes.
commonErrors.fix: Use 'Sheet Name'!A1 in the text string.

commonErrors.cause: The text string refers to the cell containing the formula.
commonErrors.fix: Restructure the formula to avoid self-reference.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: INDIRECT works similarly in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Google Sheets supports INDIRECT but cannot reference closed external sheets.

faq.question: Is INDIRECT volatile?
faq.answer: Yes, it recalculates on every change, which can slow performance.

faq.question: Can INDIRECT reference another workbook?
faq.answer: Only if the workbook is open. Closed workbooks return #REF!.

faq.question: How do I use INDIRECT with data validation?
faq.answer: Create a dropdown that selects a named range, then use INDIRECT to pull that range.
